# polytypo

> Locale-correct quotes, dashes, ellipses, hyphens and no-break spaces. One portable spec, five runtime implementations, byte-identical output — transform(input, { locale }) is pure, with no I/O, network access or global state.

polytypo is a typography rules engine, not a grammar or spell checker: it normalizes punctuation and spacing to the convention of a specific locale, and every rule cites its normative source (Chicago/Oxford, Duden, Imprimerie nationale, Kotus, Språkrådet, Мильчин). Spec 1.8.0, 19 locales (en-US, en-GB, de-DE, de-CH, fr, fr-CA, ru, fi, sv, el, es, it, pt-PT, pt-BR, nl, pl, uk, cs, tr), rules run in this fixed order: spaces, ellipsis, ranges, dashes, hyphen, quotes, apostrophe, symbols, nbsp.

Modes (4): text, html, markdown, yaml. `text` has no parser and no skip list — the whole string is prose to it. `html` and `markdown` parse the document and run the rules only on prose text nodes, never inside tags, attributes, character references, code spans or code blocks; `markdown` additionally requires an explicit `dialect` ("commonmark" or "mdx"), which is never detected, because one autolink is valid CommonMark and a parse error in MDX. `yaml` uses no parser either and is the one mode that skips by default: it processes only the values of the mapping keys named in its required `keys` option, which has no default, because nothing in YAML's syntax separates a prose `description:` from a shell command in `run:`. Whatever a mode does not process comes back byte for byte.

## Docs

- [Reference](https://polytypo.dev/docs/): API shape, options, the full error code contract, code examples for all five runtimes.
- [Error codes](https://polytypo.dev/docs/api/errors/): The eight stable polytypo error codes, when each is thrown, and why the code, not the message, is the contract.
- [Locales](https://polytypo.dev/locales/): typography rules by language, each backed by a citation and a conformance fixture set.
- [English (United States) (en-US)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/en-US/): English (United States) (en-US): quotation marks “…” and ‘…’, unspaced em dash for breaks; 11 cited sources, 340 tested examples.
- [English (United Kingdom) (en-GB)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/en-GB/): English (United Kingdom) (en-GB): quotation marks ‘…’ and “…”, spaced en dash for breaks; 9 cited sources, 165 tested examples.
- [German (Germany) (de-DE)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/de-DE/): German (Germany) (de-DE): quotation marks „…“ and ‚…‘, spaced en dash for breaks; 7 cited sources, 89 tested examples.
- [German (Switzerland) (de-CH)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/de-CH/): German (Switzerland) (de-CH): quotation marks «…» and ‹…›, spaced en dash for breaks; 6 cited sources, 61 tested examples.
- [French (fr)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/fr/): French (fr): quotation marks «…» and “…”, spaced em dash for breaks; 10 cited sources, 118 tested examples.
- [French (Canada) (fr-CA)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/fr-CA/): French (Canada) (fr-CA): quotation marks «…» and “…”, spaced em dash for breaks; 9 cited sources, 40 tested examples.
- [Russian (ru)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/ru/): Russian (ru): quotation marks «…» and „…“, spaced em dash for breaks; 6 cited sources, 89 tested examples.
- [Finnish (fi)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/fi/): Finnish (fi): quotation marks ”…” and ’…’, spaced en dash for breaks; 12 cited sources, 157 tested examples.
- [Swedish (sv)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/sv/): Swedish (sv): quotation marks ”…” and ’…’, spaced en dash for breaks; 10 cited sources, 154 tested examples.
- [Greek (el)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/el/): Greek (el): quotation marks «…» and “…”, no dash substitution for breaks; 8 cited sources, 29 tested examples.
- [Spanish (es)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/es/): Spanish (es): quotation marks «…» and “…”, no dash substitution for breaks; 10 cited sources, 23 tested examples.
- [Italian (it)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/it/): Italian (it): quotation marks «…» and “…”, spaced em dash for breaks; 10 cited sources, 21 tested examples.
- [Portuguese (Portugal) (pt-PT)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/pt-PT/): Portuguese (Portugal) (pt-PT): quotation marks «…» and “…”, spaced em dash for breaks; 8 cited sources, 19 tested examples.
- [Portuguese (Brazil) (pt-BR)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/pt-BR/): Portuguese (Brazil) (pt-BR): quotation marks “…” and ‘…’, spaced en dash for breaks; 8 cited sources, 19 tested examples.
- [Dutch (nl)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/nl/): Dutch (nl): quotation marks “…” and ‘…’, spaced en dash for breaks; 9 cited sources, 16 tested examples.
- [Polish (pl)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/pl/): Polish (pl): quotation marks „…” and »…«, spaced en dash for breaks; 9 cited sources, 16 tested examples.
- [Ukrainian (uk)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/uk/): Ukrainian (uk): quotation marks «…» and “…”, spaced em dash for breaks; 8 cited sources, 18 tested examples.
- [Czech (cs)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/cs/): Czech (cs): quotation marks „…“ and ‚…‘, spaced en dash for breaks; 8 cited sources, 19 tested examples.
- [Turkish (tr)](https://polytypo.dev/locales/tr/): Turkish (tr): quotation marks “…” and ‘…’, no dash substitution for breaks; 11 cited sources, 30 tested examples.
- [Contribute](https://polytypo.dev/contribute/): add a locale or change a rule.
- [Playground](https://polytypo.dev/playground/): run the real engine on your own text in the browser.

## Spec

- [Canonical spec repo](https://github.com/polytypo/polytypo): normative rules, locale data and conformance fixtures — runtime-agnostic, MIT licensed. An implementation is "polytypo" iff it passes this suite for the spec version it claims.
- [Modes contract](https://github.com/polytypo/polytypo/blob/main/spec/rules/modes.md): the normative document behind the modes above — the span model every mode shares, the round-trip guarantee, and each mode's skip list, including the specified scan `yaml` uses in place of a parser.
- [Conformance matrix](https://github.com/polytypo/polytypo/blob/main/spec/CONFORMANCE.md): which runtime claims which spec version, and where a runtime's claimed scope is narrower than the full spec.

## Optional

- [Manifesto](https://polytypo.dev/manifesto/): why this is typography, set by locale convention long before language models existed, not an AI watermark.
- [Changelog](https://polytypo.dev/changelog/): what changed in each released spec version, with the before-and-after of every behaviour change.
- [Sites using polytypo](https://polytypo.dev/showcase/): sites that show the polytypo badge.
